response.description:
Application
Gateway for Containers now supports private frontends that are reachable only
through approved Azure Private Link private endpoints. This enables
organizations to keep internal applications, shared services, and cross-cluster
traffic on private connectivity while retaining Kubernetes-native Layer 7
routing, TLS, health probing, and Web Application Firewall capabilities. Private ingress supports connectivity across virtual
networks, subscriptions, Microsoft Entra tenants, and Azure regions without
requiring VNet peering. A single Application Gateway for Containers resource
can also host public and private frontends, allowing teams to use separate
exposure models and security policies for different workloads. Remove the public IP
address and direct internet path from the frontend Enforce access through
explicitly provisioned and approved private endpoints  Connect workloads across VNets, subscriptions,
tenants, and regions, including environments with overlapping CIDR ranges  Place an Azure Firewall,
network virtual appliance, or another upstream service in front of Kubernetes
workloads Learn more:   Private ingress with Application
Gateway for Containers  Configure private ingress
with Application Gateway for Containers - Gateway API
response.title: Public Preview: Private ingress for Application Gateway for Containers
